Hey folks,

I’ve been saying this for months, and after watching John Fetterman’s latest interviews, I don’t feel any better about where this is headed. He says he’s never leaving the Democratic Party. Then he turns around, goes on conservative media, and attacks Democrats who are trying to win some of the most important Senate races in the country.

At some point, it’s fair to ask: what exactly is he trying to accomplish? I dig into all of it in today’s episode, and honestly, this one left me more frustrated than ever. If you care about building a Democratic majority that can actually govern, you don’t want to miss this conversation.

00:01:07 Fetterman claims he only takes issue with the “extremes,” but his latest media appearances raise bigger questions about whose arguments he’s amplifying.

00:03:06 I break down his attacks on Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and why those comments could hurt Democrats in one of the country’s most important Senate races.

00:05:22 Why campaigning as a progressive and governing as something completely different has left so many supporters feeling betrayed.

00:07:29 I examine the political reality of Fetterman’s reelection prospects and why his relationship with Republicans continues to fuel speculation.

00:10:06 The bigger picture: why Democrats need a Senate majority that’s strong enough to withstand internal defections if they’re going to stop Trump’s agenda and protect the future of the courts.

This episode is about more than one senator. It’s about trust, accountability, and what it takes to build a coalition that’s capable of winning elections and governing effectively. I talk about why party unity matters in competitive Senate races, why Democratic voters are paying attention to these fights, and why every seat could determine the future of the Supreme Court, our democracy, and the country itself.

If you value honest conversations like this—even when they’re uncomfortable—help me keep them going. Independent media only works because people like you choose to support it.

Become a paid subscriber to Endless Urgency today »

With urgency,

—Mike
